items.title: Ralph Sutton interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, September 22, 1995
items.q: I’ll never forget when I was with Bob Haggart and Yank Lawson, and it was with a band, it was called the World’s Greatest Jazz Band.

ctx.x: Oh, yeah. All the clubs, two sides of the street you know, on that side and this side. Gee, Art Tatum was playing there, and I’m trying to think. Well this was about the time too © Fillius Jazz Archive -5-

when Jack got together with Louis Armstrong and they had the Louis Armstrong All- Stars. And I’ll never forget the night I went with Jack in a taxicab over to the Town Hall where they did the, it was a Louis Armstrong concert, well he had Bobby Hackett and I think Bob Haggart played on that. And Dick Cary was playing piano, and Sid Catlett, and Peanuts was on that too. That was recorded for RCA Victor. items.title: Bob Haggart interviewed by Michael Woods, Clinton, New York, September 22, 1995
items.q: And I’ve been over since then too with a lot of the same guys, Kenny Davern and Yank Lawson and George Masso, and Ralph Sutton, and Jake Hanna.

ctx.x: Was there a time when you were expected to play both?

Oh, yeah. They’d say, “Bring both.” You’d bring them both on the job. Imagine bringing a tuba and a string bass both. There’s a guy today that, Vince Giordano, who plays the bass sax, and he brings all three. Not only that, he sets up the music stands and microphones, a PA system, plus bringing his three instruments, the string bass, the bass saxophone and a tuba. And the poor guy is very discouraged. He’s in New York but he can’t get much work for his band, and I know he’s thinking of chucking the whole thing.…
